# Template: bar_chart
A bar chart from data: categories along the x axis, one bar per category (grouped bars with `series`), drawn as ink so it animates as geometry. `values` may be one list (a static chart) or a list of lists — STAGES of the same chart — and the numeric `stage` param picks which one is shown; a fractional stage interpolates, so `animate: {stage: 1}` plays the change as bars growing and shrinking. Feed it typed numbers, or a code element's variables via "{id.var}" tokens (labels typed by hand keep the bar_i beats alive before the script has run). Choose this scene for ANY request for a bar chart, a column chart, a histogram (compute the bins in Python), a comparison across categories or years, or "show how these numbers change". Up to 200 stages, but a script's harvest caps at 5000 numbers — 20 bars × 200 stages fits, 40 × 200 does not. GUESSABLE (one series): an ask with `on: bar_2` lets the viewer drag that bar to their guess before it rises to the truth; `on: all` guesses every bar. `sort: "desc"` keeps the bars in order of their current value, so an animate between stages slides them into their new places (bar_N stays with its category).

NOTE the one asymmetry in this pack: a bar has no ABSENT state, so `null` is rejected outright when typed here, and a `null` arriving from a script counts as 0 — a bar of no height. Every other data template (line_chart, bar_race, heatmap) reads `null` as \"no value at this position\" and draws nothing there, so convert a harvested pandas `None` deliberately rather than assuming it means the same thing on both sides."

Element ids your commands can reference:
- axes: the x and y axes with their captions (and a dashed zero line when values go negative)
- bar_1: the first category's bar (its fill, outline, icon, category label and value label; bar_2, bar_3, … likewise) — one per label, at every stage
- legend: the series legend (only with several series)
- title: figure title, when set
- note: the refusal note, drawn only when a request could not be honoured
Examples:
Request: "Bar chart of GDP per capita for Norway, Sweden and Denmark." → params: {"labels":["Norway","Sweden","Denmark"],"values":[87,52,58],"y_label":"USD (thousands)","title":"GDP per capita"}
Request: "Show how the three countries' GDP changed from 2010 to 2020, one stage per year." → params: {"labels":["Norway","Sweden","Denmark"],"values":[[87,52,58],[67,52,61]],"stage":0,"value_labels":true,"title":"GDP per capita, 2010 → 2020"}
Request: "Grouped bars: treated vs control, before and after." → params: {"labels":["Before","After"],"series":[{"name":"Treated","values":[10,16]},{"name":"Control","values":[10,11]}],"y_label":"Outcome"}
Request: "Stacked bars: how total health spending splits between hospitals, primary care and drugs, 2015 vs 2020." → params: {"labels":["2015","2020"],"stacked":true,"value_labels":true,"series":[{"name":"Hospitals","values":[52,61]},{"name":"Primary care","values":[24,29]},{"name":"Drugs","values":[14,18]}],"y_label":"Billion NOK","title":"Health spending by sector"}

In YAML: `template: bar_chart` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
